name: Mind Lab Pro
summary: The most comprehensively researched nootropic stack available to Canadian buyers. Most ingredients are clinically dosed and peer-reviewed. Ships from the UK directly to Canada with reliable international delivery. Our #1 pick for the Canadian market.
whatItIs: Mind Lab Pro is an 11-ingredient pre-formulated nootropic stack sold by Performance Lab Group Ltd (Royal Leamington Spa, UK) per mindlabpro.com's terms; the brand's own posts say it was formulated by Opti-Nutra in the UK (checked 2026-10-08). It ships directly to Canada and is designed as a complete daily cognitive supplement covering memory, focus, mental energy, mood, and long-term brain health without caffeine or proprietary blends. Health Canada defines natural health products (NHPs) by substance, as "vitamins and minerals, herbal remedies, homeopathic medicines, traditional medicines (like Traditional Chinese Medicines), probiotics, and other products like amino acids and essential fatty acids", and states that "All natural health products (NHPs) sold in Canada require a product licence before being marketed." We found no NPN (Natural Product Number) for Mind Lab Pro in Health Canada's Licensed Natural Health Products Database (LNHPD) (full register export searched, 2026-10-07); the only Opti-Nutra licence-holder entry is a different, discontinued product (PhentaSlim, NPN 80068706). whatToExpect: Within 30-60 minutes: mild calm focus from L-Theanine. Within 2-4 weeks: improved mental energy and reduced cognitive fatigue. Canadian buyers pay in USD; no additional reformulation for the Canadian market. Best results require 3+ months of consistent daily use.

We found no Natural Product Number (NPN) for Performance Lab Energy or licence holder Performance Lab in Health Canada's Licensed Natural Health Products Database (LNHPD) (full register export searched, 2026-10-07); a licence can be held under another name, so look for an eight-digit NPN on the label; without one, a consumer's only route is personal importation, which Health Canada's GUI-0116 limits to "no more than a 90-day supply or a single course of treatment, whichever is less".
howItWorks: Energy is built around mitochondria, the parts of cells that turn food into usable energy. Acetyl-L-carnitine carries fatty acids into mitochondria and donates acetyl groups for making acetylcholine; its positive cognitive trials used 1.5-3g a day in older adults with mild cognitive impairment, mild dementia or pre-frailty (Montgomery 2003 meta-analysis; Passeri 1990; Malaguarnera 2022), at least three times the 500mg here, and we found no trial in healthy young adults. PQQ improved some memory and attention scores in three small 12-week trials at about 20mg a day (Itoh 2016, Shiojima 2021, Tamakoshi 2023), two of them with authors affiliated with the PQQ manufacturer; Energy has 10mg. The vendor describes CoQ10 and R-lipoic acid as mitochondrial cofactors and antioxidants, but we found no positive cognitive trial of either: 300mg CoQ10 a day did not improve attention or working memory over 6 months in a trial in schizophrenia (Maguire 2021), and 100mg alpha-lipoic acid a day did not improve cognition in the only dose-matched trial we found, also in schizophrenia (De Lima 2023). BioPerine is there to aid absorption; we have not verified whether 2.5mg of piperine changes how well these ingredients are absorbed. Energy itself has not been tested in a published trial.
whatToExpect: Performance Lab says Energy starts working in around 30 minutes and that you may notice 'increased vitality', more motivation, a brighter mood and better muscle strength and cardio performance during exercise. It contains no caffeine or other stimulant. The positive cognitive trials of acetyl-L-carnitine and PQQ ran for 12 weeks or longer at 2 to 6 times these doses, so any cognitive effect at Energy's doses is uncertain. The label suggests 2 capsules in the morning or early afternoon on an empty stomach; the product page also suggests 2 capsules 30-45 minutes before a workout. We saw only US-dollar prices ($69 one-time) when we checked.

whatItIs: Performance Lab Omega-3 is an algae-based omega-3 supplement sold through performancelab.com. The vendor positions it 'to support optimal health and performance of the brain, eyes, heart and (much) more'. One serving is 3 NutriGels, softgels the vendor describes as vegan and free of gelatin and carrageenan (other ingredients listed: gellan gum, pectin, starch and glycerin), holding 1,800mg algal oil from life's OMEGA 60 with 990mg total omega-3 fatty acids, of which 540mg is DHA and 270mg is EPA; a bottle holds 30 servings. The label suggests 3 softgels with your first meal of the day. The vendor states it is 'third-party tested for purity and potency' and Clean Label Project certified; the product page shows the certification logo but no certificate or batch number. We found no Natural Product Number (NPN) for Performance Lab Omega-3 or licence holder Performance Lab in Health Canada's Licensed Natural Health Products Database (LNHPD) (full register export searched, 2026-10-07); a licence can be held under another name, so look for an eight-digit NPN on the label; without one, a consumer's only route is personal importation, which Health Canada's GUI-0116 limits to "no more than a 90-day supply or a single course of treatment, whichever is less".
howItWorks: DHA is the main structural omega-3 in brain cell membranes. In two 6-month trials it improved memory measures at 900mg a day in adults aged 55 and over with age-related cognitive decline (Yurko-Mauro 2010, sponsored by the algal-DHA maker Martek) and at 1.16g a day in healthy 18-45-year-olds with low DHA intake (Stonehouse 2013); this product supplies 540mg, below both. The wider evidence is mixed: a 2012 Cochrane review found no cognitive benefit from omega-3 supplements in cognitively healthy older adults. We found no trial of EPA alone for cognition; a 2024 dose-response meta-analysis of 24 trials of mixed EPA and DHA in adults aged 40 and over found an executive-function benefit trend above 500mg a day of total omega-3 (Suh 2024), which the 990mg here exceeds. The oil comes from algae rather than fish, so it suits vegans. Performance Lab Omega-3 itself has not been tested in a published trial.
whatToExpect: Performance Lab says Omega-3 starts working in around 30 minutes, that you may first notice improvements to hair, nails and skin, and that other benefits build over time; both positive DHA memory trials ran for 6 months, so do not expect a quick cognitive effect. Take 3 softgels with your first meal of the day. Our DHA ingredient page notes that in a 2021 meta-analysis of cardiovascular trials, omega-3 supplements were linked to a higher risk of atrial fibrillation, more so above 1g a day; one serving here gives 990mg of total omega-3, so ask your doctor first if you have a heart-rhythm condition or already take another omega-3. We saw only US-dollar prices ($49 one-time) when we checked.
